title: Choose the visual world
question: Redesign home + projects for Huy Nguyễn’s portfolio. Copy and section order stay fixed. The roll assigned Gallery Hang — keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Gallery Hang
options.lineage: museum exhibition wall — object first, wall label second
options.thesis: Live demos hang as exhibited works; recruiters walk the rooms, labels stay quiet facts.
options.viewport: First screen is one oversized work on the wall with a short wall label (name, role) and a clear path into the hang — not a dashboard of cards.
options.risk: Can feel precious if demos are boxed like thumbnails instead of hung as large works.

raised.raise: Committed spatial voids between sections — rooms, not stacked blocks.
Empty or loading states drawn as deliberately as filled proof (ghost plates).
One off-centre calibrated rail for section wayfinding along the hang.

options.label: Specimen Sheet
options.lineage: type foundry specimen sheets — craft proved by showing the thing itself
options.thesis: Every template and demo is a live specimen of React/Next craft, printed at full scale.
options.viewport: Giant name as specimen title; skills as glyph row; projects as full-bleed specimen plates you open live.
options.risk: Also the direction many craft portfolios drift toward — familiar if executed softly.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.lineage: Łowicz layered paper roundels — depth only by stacked flat colour
options.thesis: The portfolio builds outward in paste-up layers: identity, then employers, then demos on top.
options.viewport: A symmetrical layered roundel hero; each section is another colour layer settling onto the stack.
options.case: Holds craft identification (makers recognise layered making); loses narrowly on recruiter scan clarity vs a gallery hang.
options.risk: Folk colour can overshadow the demos if layers become decoration.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: jet-age airline ticket wallet — carbon coupons, route map, stubs
options.thesis: Career as a ticket booklet: each employer a coupon, each demo a leg you tear open.
options.viewport: Open wallet with remaining journey stubs; primary CTA validates the next leg (contact).
options.case: Holds product clarity — sequential hiring scan maps cleanly to coupons; loses on craft-theatre vs gallery.
options.risk: Travel metaphor can feel gimmicky if demos are not the journey’s payload.

options.label: Bolted Manifesto
options.lineage: Futurist bolted book — diagonal wood type at engine speed
options.thesis: Frontend craft shouted as kinetic typography; demos slam in as onomatopoeic proof.
options.viewport: Name and role in colliding display type; projects enter as percussive page-slams.
options.case: Holds audience identification for craft energy; loses on recruiter calm-scan clarity.
options.risk: Motion and tilt can bury employers and contact if volume stays at shout.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: surreal cloud quarry — cut weather into temporary buildings
options.case: Recruiters do not identify with surreal quarrying; demos lose clarity inside weather metaphor.

options.label: Seven-Segment Bench
options.case: Live landing demos do not map to segment glyphs; instrument clarity fights Experience mode.
options.kept: Ghost unlit states drawn as carefully as lit proof.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: spectrogram plate on a calibrated viewing rail
options.case: Operate/science grammar undercuts a portfolio meant to be walked and felt.
options.kept: One off-centre calibrated rail for wayfinding.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Centered intro, skill pills, experience timeline, project card grid, contact form — executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Avatar + name + Contact CTA, then familiar section stack.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other frontend portfolios by design.
